baseline_comparison: Started from S19 evidence commit aeb32d8c9c49053df878657223e2fd4072d94312. The patch adds a canonical local fixture and a test-only native-insert transaction helper; production pointer behavior is unchanged. The corrected full engine run and workspace check passed. Final native CTest was rerun after the last test-helper edit and passed 59 tests.

observations: The 12-step, 200 ms left-button path selected both endpoints before press and emitted trusted pointer/mouse press, move and release events to the ordinary in-view widget.
Explicit setPointerCapture kept pointer moves on the capture widget outside its bounds and emitted capture acquisition/release events.
The canvas-like surface observed pointer moves; the native range slider changed from 10 to 94.
A 1,000 ms watchdog, Escape, input blocking and window deactivation each cleared held state and sent exactly one trusted release to the live original view.
Destroying the original QQuickView cleared owner QPointers and sent no release; the replacement view observed zero DOM events.

test_results.reason: The nested Weston startup smoke passed, but wtype could not access the compositor virtual-keyboard protocol, so native pointer input was not sent.
observations: Startup-only Wayland smoke is not treated as physical pointer qualification.
Each live-owner cancellation emitted one pointer-up and one mouse-up with trusted=true and buttons=0; no action was retried.
The range value had already changed to 94 before Escape; cleanup left it at 94 and did not claim rollback.
HTML drag produced dragstart, pointercancel and dragend, but no drop event and zero fixture drop commits. Native HTML drag-and-drop remains excluded.
After original-view destruction, no release was sent and the replacement DOM event count remained zero.

HTML drag-and-drop was excluded after observing dragstart, pointercancel and dragend without a drop in this test runner.
